subtitulo: No investigate, no tolerate — phrasal verbs for your hobby
descripcion: At C1 the issue is not knowing phrasal verbs — it is that you avoid them and reach for the Latinate synonym, which is transparent to a Spanish speaker and therefore comfortable. The result is technically correct English that sounds like a translation: *investigate* instead of *look into*, *tolerate* instead of *put up with*, *postpone* instead of *put off*. This week the Latinate options are banned.

filas: *turn off the light* / *turn the light off*
*put up with*, *come up with*, *look forward to*

ejemplos.texto: *I got into it through a friend and ended up sinking about ten years into it.*
*I've been meaning to take it back up, but I keep putting it off.*
*It started as something to wind down with and turned into a second job.*
*I can't put up with the online side of it any more.*
*I lose track of time completely when I'm tinkering with it.*

notas: Register is not uniformly informal: *carry out*, *point out* and *bring about* are fully acceptable in formal writing.
Many phrasal verbs are polysemous. *Pick up* has at least six senses; learn them by context, not by list.
Three-part verbs are the ones learners most often mangle, because the middle particle looks droppable and is not.

es.en: Spanish has no phrasal verbs, so a Spanish speaker's default retrieval is always the Latinate verb — which exists in English but sits one register higher. That mismatch, not error, is what makes advanced English sound stiff.
es.es: El español no tiene «phrasal verbs», por lo que la opción recuperada por defecto suele ser el verbo latino, que existe en inglés pero se sitúa un registro más alto. Ese desajuste, más que un error, es lo que hace que el inglés avanzado suene rígido.

de.en: German separable verbs make phrasal verbs feel natural («nachgehen» – look into), so German speakers produce them readily. The trap is similar-looking particles with different meanings («auskommen» means get by, not come out).
de.de: Deutsche trennbare Verben lassen «phrasal verbs» natürlich wirken («nachgehen» – «look into»), daher verwenden Deutschsprachige sie gern. Die Falle sind ähnlich aussehende Partikeln mit anderer Bedeutung («auskommen» heißt «get by», nicht «come out»).

it.en: Italian has its own «verbi sintagmatici» («andare avanti» – go on, «tirare fuori» – bring out), so verb + particle is a familiar idea. Italian speakers can build on these to use English phrasal verbs more actively.
it.it: L'italiano ha i propri verbi sintagmatici («andare avanti» – «go on», «tirare fuori» – «bring out»), quindi l'idea verbo + particella è familiare. Si può sfruttarla per usare più attivamente i «phrasal verbs» inglesi.

fr.en: French has no phrasal verbs, so the default is the Latinate verb («examiner» – examine), which sits one register higher than look into. That mismatch is what makes advanced English sound stiff.
fr.fr: Le français n'a pas de «phrasal verbs», donc le choix par défaut est le verbe latin («examiner» – «examine»), situé un registre au-dessus de «look into». C'est ce décalage qui rend l'anglais avancé parfois raide.

pt.en: Portuguese has no phrasal verbs, so the default is the Latinate verb («investigar» – investigate), which sits one register higher than look into. That mismatch is what makes advanced English sound stiff.
pt.pt: O português não tem «phrasal verbs», então a opção padrão é o verbo latino («investigar» – «investigate»), que fica um registro acima de «look into». Esse desajuste é o que faz o inglês avançado soar rígido.

errores: *Discuss about* — no preposition. Contrast with *talk about*.
Pronoun after the particle: *turn on it*.
Defaulting to the Latinate verb, which is the whole point this week.

es: «*sacar adelante*» rendered as *take forward* instead of *pull through* or *see through*.
de: «*durchziehen*» rendered as *pull through*, which means 'survive', instead of *see through* or *push through*.
it: «*portare avanti*» rendered as *bring forward*, which means 'move earlier', instead of *carry on with* or *press ahead with*.
fr: «*mener à bien*» rendered as *lead to well* instead of *see through* or *carry out*.
pt: «*levar adiante*» rendered as *carry ahead* instead of *carry on with* or *press ahead with*.

vocabulario.item: to take the fun out of something
to turn a hobby into a job

traducciones.fr: faire de sa passion un métier

vocabulario.item: to keep it just a hobby

redemittel.expresion: to take up / take back up

traducciones.de: sich etwas ausdenken / auf etwas kommen

mision.consigna: Tell the story of how a hobby started, grew and maybe turned into something more.
requisitos: six phrasal verbs from the reference box
no Latinate synonym where a phrasal fits
use *a side hustle*, *to plateau* and *to turn a hobby into a job*

microtareas.texto: Write five sentences with Latinate verbs about your hobby, then swap each for a phrasal.
Write about something you *put off* and later *took back up*.
Record 90 seconds: does money *take the fun out of* a hobby?

autochequeo: Twelve different phrasal verbs — count them.
Any pronoun sitting after a particle?
Did I split a three-part verb?
Did any Latinate verb slip through?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on phrasal verbs. (1) List each one and check the particle and the separation. (2) Flag every Latinate verb where a phrasal one would sound more natural, and give it. (3) Flag any register mismatch. (4) Check pronoun placement. Do not rewrite the text.
